# TEMPORARY LLM-GENERATED DONT EDIT YET What's New in the ALMA Pipeline 2026

This document summarizes ALMA-relevant development on the
[`PIPE/pipeline`](https://open-bitbucket.nrao.edu/projects/PIPE/repos/pipeline/browse)
repository between October 2025 and August 2026, drawn from the 209 pull
requests merged in that window. VLA/VLASS/AUDI-only work, regression-test
maintenance, and MAIN-branch backport ("clone") tickets are omitted; related
tickets are grouped into single feature entries with a short summary of the
underlying change (not just the ticket title) and links to the source PIPE
tickets.

Sections are organized as: ALMA-IF Calibration, ALMA-IF Imaging, ALMA-SD, and
Infrastructure, with QA-score and weblog/plot work pulled into its own
section at the end, ordered to follow the
[`hifa_polcalimage`](https://pipe-docs.readthedocs.io/en/docs-update-pl2026/users_guide/hifa_polcalimage-recipe.html)
and
[`hsd_calimage`](https://pipe-docs.readthedocs.io/en/docs-update-pl2026/users_guide/hsd_calimage-recipe.html)
recipes so a user following either recipe can see, stage by stage, what
changed.


## ALMA-IF Calibration

### Low-SNR calibration workflow unification around `ALMAPhcorBandpass`

Several stages historically used two different bandpass/phase-up code paths:
the generic {func}`hif_bandpass <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_bandpass>` "PhcorBandpass"
worker, and the ALMA-specific "ALMAPhcorBandpass" worker used by
{func}`hifa_bandpass <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_bandpass>`, which supports
spw-combined solves and longer solution intervals for low-SNR data. This
cycle's work switched {func}`hif_lowgainflag <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_lowgainflag>`
over to the ALMA-specific worker so ALMA low-SNR data benefit from the same
combine/solint handling as bandpass itself
([PIPE-2601](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2601)), then closed out a
regression this introduced — a missing "phase offset" solve ahead of the
post-bandpass phase-up when `combine='spw'` is triggered, which had been
causing worse flagging than before
([PIPE-3139](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3139)). A related fix
extended the requirement to use `interp='linearPD'` interpolation to every
calibration stage that can trigger `combine='spw'` low-SNR solves —
{func}`hifa_bandpass <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_bandpass>`,
{func}`hifa_bandpassflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_bandpassflag>`,
{func}`hifa_diffgaincal <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_diffgaincal>`,
{func}`hifa_gfluxscale <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscale>`,
{func}`hifa_gfluxscaleflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscaleflag>`, and
{func}`hifa_timegaincal <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_timegaincal>`
([PIPE-2858](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2858)). Finally,
{func}`hifa_wvrgcalflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_wvrgcalflag>` — the *first*
stage in the recipe to run a bandpass/phase-up solve — was brought into the
same low-SNR heuristic, since it previously used unconditional short
`solint='int'` solves that could fail outright on weak calibrators
([PIPE-3006](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3006)).

![Updated hifa_wvrgcalflag low-SNR solve sequence, showing where the phase-offset and combine='spw' logic now sits in the flow][pipe3006_wvrgcal_flow]

### Band-to-band (B2B) `hifa_diffgaincal` robustness

Band-to-band observations solve the DIFFGAIN offset from two interleaved
scan "blocks" at the start and end of the observation. Two crash/flagging
bugs in this logic were fixed: {func}`hifa_diffgaincal <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_diffgaincal>`
would crash outright via a {func}`CASA/gaincal <casatasks.calibration.gaincal>`
`append=True` call if the *first* scan-group block was fully flagged, since
there was no gaintable yet to append to
([PIPE-2915](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2915)); separately, if
only the *second* block was fully flagged, the calflag apply logic dropped
all TARGET/CHECK solutions after the end of the first block's timestamp,
flagging science data that should have been recoverable from the first
block's solution alone
([PIPE-2932](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2932)).

### Polarization calibration recipe fixes

In the polarization calibration recipe, the second
{func}`hifa_bandpass <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_bandpass>` solve (run after
{func}`hifa_lock_refant <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_lock_refant>` re-locks the
reference antenna) was still pre-applying the *first* spw-phase-offset table
from the earlier {func}`hifa_spwphaseup <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_spwphaseup>`
stage instead of picking up the refreshed one made after the antenna change —
the first table is now de-registered so only the current offset table is
used ([PIPE-3016](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3016)). A Band 2
full-polarization dataset also exposed a case where the co-polarization sum
(XX+YY) was flat versus time but the cross-polarization sum (XY+YX) was not,
which the multi-scan-calibrator flagging in
{func}`hifa_gfluxscaleflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscaleflag>` and
{func}`hifa_polcalflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_polcalflag>` had assumed could
not happen; a new `examineCrossPolSum` parameter (default `False`) now lets
these stages skip the cross-pol examination pending a longer-term fix
([PIPE-2956](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2956)). A smaller,
related fix corrected a `str`-vs-`bool` typo for the `doquantiles` argument
passed to {func}`CASA/visstat <casatasks.information.visstat>` in
{func}`hifa_polcal <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_polcal>`
([PIPE-2166](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2166),
[PIPE-3070](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3070)).

![hifa_lock_refant: the stale spw-phase-offset table is now de-registered before the post-lock bandpass re-solve][pipe3016_lockrefant]

### Bandpass/flux-scale SNR heuristics: documentation and follow-up fixes

Two smaller efforts cleaned up the SNR-scaling code shared by
{func}`hifa_bandpass <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_bandpass>` and
{func}`hifa_gfluxscale <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscale>`: an out-of-bounds
error in the ATM-line-fitting extrapolation used by the bandpass subband QA
scoring was fixed, and its QA messaging was made to aggregate by amplitude
and phase separately rather than by spw alone
([PIPE-2845](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2845)); separately, the
`snr.py` heuristics code had a variable that was really "number of antennas
minus one" but was named and treated as "number of baselines" — the code now
carries explanatory comments on the fiducial-sensitivity scaling so future
developers don't have to reverse-engineer it
([PIPE-2901](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2901)).

### `hifa_flagdata` FDM-spectral-window detection and memory use

The heuristic that decides whether a spectral window is FDM (full spectral
resolution) or TDM in {func}`hifa_flagdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_flagdata>`
compared channel count against a fixed threshold, which mis-identified
2023-cycle-10-era 4x4-bit-correlation FDM windows with heavy online averaging
as TDM and applied the wrong edge-flagging fraction. The heuristic now uses
`msmd.almaspws(fdm=True)` metadata directly, falling back to the old
channel-count heuristic only when metadata is unavailable
([PIPE-2320](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2320)). Separately, the
partial-polarization flagging loop in `flagdeteralma` was found to load the
entire FLAG column per spw/scan/DDID via table-tool `getcol()`, producing
short-lived multi-GB memory ramps on wide-band data; it now uses a TaQL
query instead, with no change to flagging results
([PIPE-3023](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3023)).

![ALMA FDM spectral windows are now identified via msmd.almaspws() CASA metadata instead of a fixed channel-count threshold][pipe2320_fdmspws]

### Flux calibrator catalog query robustness (`hifa_importdata`)

Three fixes hardened {func}`hifa_importdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_importdata>`'s
interaction with the online Source Catalogue flux service: the pipeline now
halts with an informative QA message (instead of silently continuing with a
red score) if both the primary and backup flux-service URLs fail to answer a
test query ([PIPE-2127](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2127)); a race
condition in the MPI-parallel import path — where one process could release
its file lock on `flux.csv` before its write buffer had actually flushed to
Lustre, handing a second process an incomplete header line — was fixed by
flushing before unlocking ([PIPE-3099](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3099));
and the Source Catalogue flux XML parser, which previously counted columns
by fixed position, now reads fields by name so it survives the Source
Catalogue team adding or reordering columns
([PIPE-3101](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3101)).

### `hifa_importdata` performance

Validation testing showed import taking noticeably longer than the prior
release; profiling traced most of the regression to
`compute_zd_telmjd_for_ms`, which recomputed per-field zenith-angle/MJD
values inside a Python loop. The function was vectorized and its unused
`zd`/`telmjd` outputs on the `Field` object were removed, cutting import
time by roughly 20% on the tested measurement set
([PIPE-3088](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3088)).

### `hifa_exportdata` bug fixes

Two independent bugs in export were fixed. First, the second call to
{func}`hifa_exportdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_exportdata>` at the end of the
imaging stages was writing its flag backup to the same `Pipeline_Final`
{func}`CASA/flagmanager <casatasks.flagging.flagmanager>` version name as the
first (post-calibration) call, silently renaming the pre-imaging flag backup
to a timestamped `.old.*` version instead of preserving it under its own
name ([PIPE-2274](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2274)). Second, for
MOUSes with a representative bandwidth (RepBW) spw, exportdata's
deduplication logic was resolving both the repBW image and the full-bandwidth
cube image to the same `specmode`, so the cube was discarded as a duplicate
and never delivered; images are now registered with the pipeline's actual
specmode to disambiguate them
([PIPE-3012](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3012), applied to MAIN in
[PIPE-3018](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3018)).

### `hifa_imageprecheck` sensitivity fix

{func}`hifa_imageprecheck <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_imageprecheck>` could build
a duplicated virtual-spw continuum list from the representative-target
field's metadata, biasing the aggregate-bandwidth sensitivity estimate low
for affected datasets (the beam calculation was unaffected because it already
deduplicated spws before PSF fitting). The continuum spw list is now
deduplicated before being used in the sensitivity calculation
([PIPE-3090](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3090)).

### Calibration-task performance: fewer repeated MS opens

Several calibration tasks were repeatedly opening and closing the
measurement-set tool inside inner loops —
{func}`hifa_fluxcalflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_fluxcalflag>`'s per-line
frequency-to-channel conversion, and
{func}`hif_applycal <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_applycal>` weblog rendering, which
was reopening the MS once per field × spw × EB (roughly 50 minutes of
overhead on a large mosaic test case). These, along with
{func}`hif_rawflagchans <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_rawflagchans>`,
`correctedampflag`, and
{func}`hifa_gfluxscale <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscale>`'s
`gcorfluxscale`, now reuse a single MS handle across their inner loops
([PIPE-3085](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3085)).

### `hifa_tsysflagcontamination` robustness

Two crash fixes: a newer scipy's `savgol_filter` implementation behaved
differently around NaN-masked regions than the pipeline's reference
environment, crashing the smoothing step used in Tsys-contamination
heuristics — the code now pads NaNs around masked regions itself rather than
relying on scipy's edge handling
([PIPE-2947](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2947)); and
{func}`hifa_tsysflagcontamination <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_tsysflagcontamination>`
crashed on measurement sets whose basename didn't start with `uid`, which
the internal `TsysDataClassFile` regex assumed
([PIPE-3115](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3115)).

## ALMA-IF Imaging

### `hif_selfcal` robustness and performance

Four fixes to self-calibration: a regression where mosaic + single-pol
datasets interacted badly — a prior fix for single-pol flagging reporting had
switched `gaincal` back to `gaintype='G'`, so both polarizations ended up in
the solution table, and `hif_selfcal`'s mosaic logic then dropped *every*
solution with a flag in either polarization, crashing self-cal — was
resolved by using `gaintype='T'` for single-pol data again in the inf_EB
trial ([PIPE-2908](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2908)); the
near-field SNR estimation in `auto_selfcal.estimate_near_field_SNR` could
write out as many as 13 large temporary images per call, which under
concurrent selfcal workers could pressure node page-cache into swapping —
this was refactored to use in-memory `ia`-tool images instead of temp files,
with a matching optimization to the noise-histogram display code
([PIPE-2937](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2937)); a serial
model-write workaround for a CASA `mosaic`-gridder bug (fixed upstream in
CASA 6.6.5) was removed now that it's no longer needed
([PIPE-3025](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3025)); and a stale
"mosaic is a new mode" QA message was removed now that mosaic self-cal is
long-established ([PIPE-3147](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3147)).

### `hif_findcont` / continuum-imaging pipeline refactor

`findContinuum.py` — the shared continuum-range-finding algorithm — was
updated to v9.6 ([PIPE-2766](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2766)).
{func}`hif_findcont <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_findcont>` was also refactored to
build its own dirty-cube target list via an intrinsic call to
{func}`hif_makeimlist <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_makeimlist>` rather than reusing
the context's externally-populated `clean_list_pending`, removing an
implicit recipe-ordering dependency and letting `hif_findcont` apply its own
local imaging-parameter overrides (e.g. `robust=1` for smaller findcont
cubes) directly ([PIPE-3131](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3131)).
This introduced a new `hm_mode` parameter with a `'coarse'` (reduced
pixels-per-beam, faster) and `'normal'` (previous-cycle behavior) option;
after feedback that defaulting to `'coarse'` had unintended consequences for
some users, the default was changed back to `'normal'`, with ALMA recipes now
explicitly requesting `hm_mode='coarse'` where the speed-up is wanted
([PIPE-3209](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3209)). Independently, a
plain bug fix: `hif_findcont` was not forwarding the `uvrange` set by a prior
{func}`hif_makeimlist <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_makeimlist>` into its internal
{func}`CASA/tclean <casatasks.imaging.tclean>` call, so per-target UV range
restrictions were silently ignored during continuum finding
([PIPE-2617](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2617)).

![findContinuum.py v9.6 documentation/reference update][pipe2766_findcontinuum]

![hif_findcont now forwards a target-specific uvrange into its internal tclean call][pipe2617_findcont_uvrange]

### `hif_uvcontsub` for the new LSRK imaging-MS data type

To support the new `IM_CONTLINE_SCIENCE` imaging-MS data type (created in
LSRK frame by a second `mstransform`),
{func}`hif_uvcontsub <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_uvcontsub>` was extended to derive
frequency and channel ranges in frames other than the TOPO frame it
previously assumed, enabling LSRK-frame IF imaging (REST/SOURCE-frame support
was deferred pending a `mstransform` limitation)
([PIPE-3057](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3057)). Separately, a
performance bug where `hif_uvcontsub` could run for multiple days during a
restore — because continuum-mitigation-limited field selection wasn't
respected, so the task iterated needlessly over fields with no continuum
ranges, generating a 10+ GB log in the process — was fixed by scoping the
loop to the mitigated field/spw selection
([PIPE-2952](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2952)).

### New `hif_findroi` region-of-interest stage

A new pipeline stage, {func}`hif_findroi <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_findroi>`,
was implemented to quickly identify a target's region of interest ahead of
imaging, based on prior research
([PIPE-3149](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3149)) and added to the
ALMA imaging recipes ahead of continuum finding
([PIPE-3151](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3151)). A follow-up
security fix removed pipeline-host filesystem paths that the stage's pickled
output and its aux-products tarball had been leaking to users
([PIPE-3191](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3191); weblog work for
this stage is covered in the QA and Weblog section below).

### Full-polarization (Stokes IQUV) imaging fixes

Two bugs in polarization-calibration imaging: a lookup-key mismatch (quoted
vs. unquoted field names, and field-selection string vs. resolved source
name) meant that `context.clean_masks`/`clean_thresholds` lookups could
silently return `None`, so the second (RepBW Stokes IQUV) imaging pass would
fail to reuse the clean mask/threshold established by the Stokes-I RepBW pass
([PIPE-3096](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3096),
[PIPE-3128](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3128)).

### `hif_checkproductsize` spw filtering for size mitigation

When both the max-cube-size and max-product-size mitigation steps fail
because no spw filter was available, the whole mitigation could fail outright
even though some data — just not the largest cube — was imageable. A new spw
filter now limits imaging to the representative spw and others that fit
within the size budget, so mitigation degrades gracefully instead of failing
([PIPE-3127](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3127)).

![Updated max-cube-size / max-product-size mitigation flow with SpW filtering added at each step][pipe3127_mitigation_flow]

### Multi-EB check-source export fix

For MOUSes with multiple EBs observing the same check source,
{func}`hifa_exportdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_exportdata>`'s
deduplication key didn't include the EB UID, so only the last-observed EB's
check-source images were exported instead of all of them (a regression from
PL2024 behavior). The EB UID is now part of the deduplication key
([PIPE-3074](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3074)).

## ALMA-SD

### `hsd_atmcor` parallelization and atmospheric-type heuristic

{func}`hsd_atmcor <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_atmcor>` was converted to a Tier-0
(MPI) parallel task; because {func}`CASA/sdatmcor <casatasks.single.sdatmcor>`
uses OpenMP internally and `mpicasa` already forces `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, this
was safe to enable without threading conflicts
([PIPE-1781](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-1781)). Separately, the
heuristic that selects the best-fit atmospheric-line "atmtype" was found to
sometimes pick a worse-fitting type than the prior release; the scoring
metric was changed from a total-variation-like "intabsdiff" measure to an
"intsqdiff" measure that better penalizes sharp residual features
([PIPE-2774](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2774)).

![hsd_atmcor Tier-0 (mpicasa) parallel execution, confirmed to use multiple cores per EB][pipe1781_tier0]

![hsd_atmcor atmtype heuristic fix: PL2025 (top) vs. the corrected fit][pipe2774_atmtype]

### `hsd_baseline` fitting options and bug fixes

{func}`hsd_baseline <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_baseline>` gained a `sinusoid`
fitting function (in addition to polynomial/Chebyshev), with a new
`wavenumber` parameter accepting a single value, a per-spw dictionary, or
per-EB lists/dicts of either
([PIPE-2893](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2893)), and its sparse
profile-map plots now always show a channel axis on the top panel — a
Nobeyama-only feature previously — for ALMA data too
([PIPE-2894](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2894)). Two bugs were
also fixed: k-means clustering in the line-detection step crashed when fewer
lines were detected than the requested cluster count, now skipped safely in
that case ([PIPE-2695](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2695)); and a
confusion between "virtual" and "real" spw ids in `baseline/worker.py` broke
processing of multi-EB datasets with varying real-spw assignments
([PIPE-3001](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3001)).

![hsd_baseline sinusoid fitting option: with (left) vs. without sinusoid fitting][pipe2893_sinusoid]

![hsd_baseline sparse profile map: channel axis now always shown on the top panel][pipe2894_channelaxis]

### `hsd_imaging` output correctness

{func}`hsd_imaging <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_imaging>` now sets
{func}`CASA/tsdimaging <casatasks.single.tsdimaging>`'s `stokes` parameter to
`"I"` directly rather than the historical `"pseudoI"` workaround, now that
CASA changes (CAS-9957/CAS-14444) make the two produce identical images —
this removes a source of confusion in the code without changing output
([PIPE-2490](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2490)). A performance
fix skips the `WeightMS` subtask's redundant recomputation of the MS weight
column, since {func}`CASA/sdbaseline <casatasks.single.sdbaseline>`'s
weight-column update (from baseline standard deviation) was shown to already
match it ([PIPE-2491](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2491)). A
channel-range bug for moment maps (mom0/mom8) in LSB spws — where the
frequency axis is flipped but the line-free-channel-range computation didn't
account for it — was also fixed
([PIPE-3141](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3141)), along with a
warning-message typo ("futher" → "further")
([PIPE-2954](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2954)).

### `hsd_k2jycal` backup Jy/K database URL

{func}`hsd_k2jycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_k2jycal>` now uses a new
`getjyperkalma` task to query the Jy/K conversion-factor database, with
automatic fallback through a list of backup URLs (JAO → NA → EU → EA) if the
configured primary URL is unreachable, instead of failing outright
([PIPE-2967](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2967)).

### `hsd_skycal` fault tolerance

{func}`hsd_skycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_skycal>` previously crashed the
whole SD pipeline if {func}`CASA/sdcal <casatasks.single.sdcal>` failed to
build a sky caltable for even one science target (typically because that
target had no valid OFF_SOURCE data) — it now consolidates the per-target
`sdcal` calls and catches per-target failures, allowing the run to continue
with the remaining valid targets
([PIPE-2945](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2945)).

### `hsd_applycal` refactoring

Follow-up refactoring from PIPE-2168 removed hardcoded filenames and
duplicated x/y-axis logic between `hsd/tasks/applycal/display.py` and the QA
score calculator, improving filename consistency between the two
([PIPE-2718](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2718)).

### `hsd_importdata` off-position naming

An old ALMA-commissioning-era absolute-off-position naming convention
(`Target_0`) could be misidentified as both an OFF position *and* an
independent science target; {func}`hsd_importdata <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_importdata>`
now prefers matching a relative OFF field (identical name to the ON field)
before falling back to the absolute-OFF naming convention
([PIPE-3167](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3167)).

### `hsd_exportdata` / NRO image products

A per-antenna (beam) XXYY image-product deduplication key was missing the
antenna name, so some per-beam FITS products were silently dropped from NRO
(Nobeyama) Pipeline output since PL2025; the antenna name is now part of the
key ([PIPE-3129](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3129)).

### SD Tier-0 parallel-framework fix

`ParallelTemplate`'s worker-argument distribution assumed the scope
attribute for per-EB parameters was always named `vis`, which broke Tier-0
parallel dispatch for SD tasks that use `infiles` instead; the distribution
logic now respects each task's actual scope attribute
([PIPE-3035](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3035)).

### `hsd_flagdata` pointing-outlier heuristic

Pointing-outlier detection previously ran separately per antenna, so when
the majority of one antenna's otherwise-valid pointing data happened to
cluster away from the rest, the heuristic could flag it as an outlier
antenna-by-antenna. Detection now combines pointing data from all antennas
before identifying outliers, which is more robust when only one antenna out
of several is actually affected
([PIPE-3119](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3119)).

### SD pointing-data fix at RA = 12h

SDPL could not handle pointing distributions that straddle RA = 12h, because
CASA's `measures` tool returns RA in (−180°, +180°] and a raster map centered
near RA=12h could split into two disjoint clusters at the wrap. RA (and
`SHIFT_RA`, `OFS_RA`, and AZ where relevant) are now unwrapped consistently
before use ([PIPE-2913](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2913)).

![RA=12h pointing-wrap fix: channel map before (left) vs. after the fix][pipe2913_ra12h]

## Infrastructure

### Python/library compatibility and deprecation cleanup

Ongoing compatibility work kept the pipeline running against newer
dependency releases: NumPy 2.4 removed deprecated APIs used by the pipeline
(`np.in1d`, 0-d array-to-scalar coercion, the `percentile`/`quantile`
`interpolation` keyword), addressed incrementally starting with the
`np.in1d` → `np.isin` migration
([PIPE-2930](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2930)); a matplotlib
3.11+ `AttributeError` in a custom colormap wrapper (`_SentinelMap`) was
fixed by properly delegating to `Colormap.__init__()`
([PIPE-3116](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3116)); and a batch of
matplotlib/NumPy/pyparsing deprecation warnings surfaced by regression-test
output were cleaned up
([PIPE-1836](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-1836)), along with a
specific `AntennaArray.baselines` deprecation warning that was leaking into
casalog even during SD-only runs
([PIPE-2209](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2209)), a scipy<1.5
MAD-computation compatibility wrapper that's no longer needed
([PIPE-2912](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2912)), and an
explicit `me.done()` call after `me.doframe()` transforms plus a time-cache
clear after `importasdm`, guarding against stateful behavior in the CASA
`measures` tool ([PIPE-2891](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2891)).

### CI/CD and developer tooling

A GitHub Actions workflow now mirrors `main` from the on-prem Bitbucket repo
to the public GitHub mirror
([PIPE-2995](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2995)); the unit-test
workflow now caches `casarundata` to reduce network traffic and flakiness
when the measures-data server is unavailable
([PIPE-2996](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2996)); the unit-test
matrix was expanded across more CASA/Python version combinations, migrating
to a pixi-based environment setup
([PIPE-2997](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2997)); a new
top-level `scripts/` directory now hosts standalone developer/CI helpers,
starting with a script that produces a parallel-enabled copy of a procedure
XML for faster regression runs
([PIPE-3063](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3063)); and GitHub
Copilot custom repository instructions were added to steer AI-assisted code
review toward the project's Python conventions (e.g. the 3.10-compatibility
requirement) ([PIPE-2935](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2935)).

### Documentation modernization

The developer- and user-facing documentation received a substantial
overhaul this cycle: a restructuring and visual/theme migration of the
Sphinx build, a switch of the Read the Docs build to pixi after
`environment.yaml` was retired, and several rounds of content consolidation
and fixes, all tracked under one umbrella epic
([PIPE-2738](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2738)). Developer docs
were also updated to reflect that `context = pipeline.Pipeline().context`
no longer works and `context = launcher.Pipeline().context` should be used
instead ([PIPE-2985](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2985)), a new
document was written covering practical use cases and limitations of the
pipeline `Context` object
([PIPE-3079](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3079)), and the Read the
Docs version-string formatting was cleaned up (dropping a spurious
`-dirty` suffix and a tag that was confusing the release-branch lookup)
([PIPE-3195](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3195)).

### Recipe auto-generation

Manually-maintained recipe scripts (`hifacal.py`, `hifatargets.py`, `hsd.py`,
etc.) were replaced with scripts auto-generated from the procedure XML files
by an updated `recipe_converter.py`, removing a source of drift between the
XML procedures and the Python recipes that wrap them
([PIPE-1263](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-1263)).

### Code modernization and refactoring

A broad pass modernized type hints to PEP 484/585/604 style and removed
defunct infrastructure modules
([PIPE-2903](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2903)); redundant helper
functions left behind in `htmlrenderer.py` after an earlier refactor
(PIPE-2307) were removed in favor of the equivalent `MeasurementSet` methods
([PIPE-2934](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2934)); and
`rendererutils.num_lines()` was fixed to close its file handle instead of
leaking the descriptor ([PIPE-3015](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3015)).

### Licensing

An LGPL v3 `LICENSE.md` file was added at the top level (replacing
per-file license headers), later updated to include the ALMA partnership,
ESO, and NAOJ in the copyright notice
([PIPE-1001](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-1001)).

### Parallel/MPI correctness

Under `parallel=True`, data-product filenames (caltables, images, etc.)
created on MPI workers could omit the registered pipeline task name (e.g.
`.hifa_gfluxscale.`) because the serial task class used on workers isn't
registered in `task_registry`, causing caltable filenames to differ between
serial and parallel runs for the same task — the task name is now resolved
consistently on workers too
([PIPE-3089](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3089)). Separately, when
running with `loglevel='debug'`, the pipeline now saves its per-stage
context snapshot *before* weblog rendering rather than after, so a weblog
rendering failure can be debugged from the pickled context without rerunning
the stage ([PIPE-2980](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2980)).

## QA and Weblog Improvements

This section covers every QA-score and weblog/plot change in the window,
ordered to follow the ALMA
[`hifa_polcalimage`](https://pipe-docs.readthedocs.io/en/docs-update-pl2026/users_guide/hifa_polcalimage-recipe.html)
recipe and then the
[`hsd_calimage`](https://pipe-docs.readthedocs.io/en/docs-update-pl2026/users_guide/hsd_calimage-recipe.html)
recipe, so a user following either recipe stage-by-stage can see what changed
in the weblog and AQUA report at each step.

### ALMA IF (`hifa_polcalimage` order)

**{func}`hifa_importdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_importdata>` / measurement-set overview.**
The "Spatial Setup Details" page now plots, per EB, the on-sky separation
angle between each TARGET (and CHECK) field and the PHASE calibrator, with a
summary table (for ≥5 targets, showing only the closest/farthest pairs) and
per-source-pair scores propagated into the AQUA report — a long-standing
request so data analysts don't have to compute phase-transfer separation
angles by hand
([PIPE-65](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-65)). The measurement-set
overview's "Spectral Setup Details" page now shows two additional columns,
Resolution in MHz and km/s, alongside the existing channel-width columns,
since resolution and width are only equal from Cycle 3 onward
([PIPE-117](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-117)). Source-pointing
plots that had gone missing for multi-target datasets in the Spatial Setup
Details page — anywhere a target lacked its own Tsys measurement — are
restored via a fallback that plots the closest target-mapped Tsys field
([PIPE-3163](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3163)), and a related
weblog-rendering bug for datasets where a polarization-calibration field was
present in one EB of a session but not another was fixed
([PIPE-3002](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3002)). A formatting bug
in the AQUA report — where single-string values like the ASDM/EB name were
iterated character-by-character and joined with commas (`u,i,d,...`) instead
of being treated as one string — was also fixed
([PIPE-3034](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3034)).

![Source pointing / TARGET–PHASE separation-angle plot added to the weblog and AQUA report][pipe65_sepangle]

**Tsys calibration weblog.** The Tsys ON_SOURCE/TEST-scan comparison plot
(introduced in PIPE-2613) is only meaningful for Cycle 3+ data, where the
AtmCal subscan intents changed from `#ON_SOURCE` to `#HOT`/`#AMBIENT`; the
cycle check now prefers the software-version string over the nominal PI
science-start date, and a related dictionary-key-type/field-name-matching
bug from the same code was cleaned up
([PIPE-2698](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2698)).

**{func}`hifa_wvrgcalflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_wvrgcalflag>` QA score.**
For ACA data with only 3–4 usable PM antennas, a single flagged PM antenna
used to trigger the same red "insufficient antennas" score as a genuine
40+-antenna-flagged failure on the main array; this case is now scored
yellow instead, with an additional check that raises the score to blue if
the BANDPASS calibrator's phase RMS is already good enough that the missing
WVR solution doesn't matter
([PIPE-1868](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-1868)).

**{func}`hifa_gfluxscale <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscale>` / {func}`hifa_gfluxscaleflag <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_gfluxscaleflag>` QA.**
A new QA subscore evaluates calibrated amplitude-vs-time variation for each
non-SSO flux calibrator (using the highest-S/N spw from the
{func}`hifa_spwphaseup <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_spwphaseup>` mapping), turning
yellow when the difference between the top and bottom amplitude quintiles
relative to the median exceeds a threshold — intended to flag EBs whose flux
scale may be compromised for possible QA0 semi-pass consideration
([PIPE-2553](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2553)). A separate crash
— `min() arg is an empty sequence` — hit Band-to-Band datasets without a
CHECK intent, where the QA code unconditionally assumed one; it now returns
`None` and lets the existing early-warning path handle the missing field
([PIPE-2694](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2694)).

**{func}`hifa_timegaincal <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_timegaincal>` QA score.**
Analysis of "false positive" slow-lane QA0 outcomes found that phase-offset
outliers in *unmapped* spws were being scored yellow (0.5) when they don't
meaningfully affect science data; the score for this case is now blue (0.75),
increasing the fraction of data eligible for fast-lane delivery without
loosening detection of genuinely bad data
([PIPE-3026](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3026)).

**{func}`hifa_flagdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_flagdata>` QA score.**
Following the same false-positive analysis, the QA score thresholds for
percent-flagged data were shifted (`f_low`/`f_up` raised by 0.19 each) so
that flagging levels which previously landed just inside "yellow" now land
in "blue," matching where the analysis showed no material change in delivered
data quality ([PIPE-3036](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3036)).

**{func}`hif_applycal <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_applycal>` QA and QA-support files.**
The same threshold shift was applied to the "newly flagged by applycal"
score ([PIPE-3037](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3037)), and the
`applycalQA_outliers.txt` support file used to investigate Amp/Phase-vs-Freq
QA outliers now includes the calibration intent for every scan, making it
possible to identify outlying data without cross-referencing scan numbers by
hand; the `PIPE356_QA_MODE` environment-variable switch from the original
implementation was also retired in favor of always-on continuous scoring
([PIPE-2716](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2716)).

**{func}`hif_makeimlist <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_makeimlist>` / {func}`hif_makeimages <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_makeimages>` QA and AQUA report.**
Three AQUA-report additions: the non-primary-beam-corrected image peak/min
flux (`ImageMaxJyPerBeam`/`ImageMinJyPerBeam`), useful for e.g. evaluating
self-calibration progress, alongside the existing PB-corrected values
([PIPE-2073](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2073)); the multiterm
(`.tt0.`) extension in reported image names, which had been dropped from the
`<Sensitivity>` entries for multiterm imaging runs
([PIPE-2489](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2489)); and, for
full-polarization imaging runs, per-Stokes-plane (I/Q/U/V) sensitivity
statistics instead of Stokes-I only
([PIPE-3014](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3014)). On the QA-score
side, the check-source-fit aggregation in `hif_makeimages` no longer folds in
the image-to-gfluxscale flux-ratio subscore, which was found to turn yellow
even on otherwise-unremarkable check-source results
([PIPE-3042](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3042)); and, for the
representative-bandwidth (RepBW) cube specifically, the `mom8fc` contamination
subscore is no longer folded into the overall stage score, since findcont
frequency ranges routinely include line emission at RepBW's coarser
resolution even when the full-bandwidth cube's `mom8fc` score is fine
([PIPE-3082](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3082)).

![RepBW mom8fc contamination subscore is no longer folded into the overall hif_makeimages QA score][pipe3082_mom8fc]

**{func}`hif_findcont <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_findcont>` weblog.**
After PIPE-3131 moved target-imaging setup out of a separate
{func}`hif_makeimlist <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_makeimlist>` stage and into
`hif_findcont` itself, and introduced the `'coarse'`/`'normal'` `hm_mode`,
those decisions had become invisible in the weblog. The `hif_findcont`
weblog page now shows the imaging parameters directly, denotes coarse vs.
normal mode and the pixels-per-beam used, and updates the methodology text
accordingly ([PIPE-3159](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3159)).

**New {func}`hif_findroi <pipeline.hif.cli.hif_findroi>` weblog.**
Following the initial implementation of the region-of-interest stage
(PIPE-3149), its weblog view was substantially improved — clearer
field/spw-level presentation, better plotting diagnostics, and QA/failure
handling that distinguishes "no data" from "plotting failed" so users aren't
left guessing why a panel is blank
([PIPE-3150](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3150)); its output
tarball is now included in {func}`hifa_exportdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_exportdata>`'s
aux-products tarball
([PIPE-3136](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3136)).

**{func}`hifa_exportdata <pipeline.hifa.cli.hifa_exportdata>` AQUA report.**
The ASDM/EB UIDs for a dataset are now recorded in the AQUA report's Project
Structure header (previously only visible per-stage in the
`hifa_importdata` QA section), which the Fast Feedback per-EB calibration
workflow needs to identify which EB was processed
([PIPE-2470](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2470)).

![EB/ASDM UIDs added to the pipeline_aquareport.xml Project Structure header][pipe2470_ebuid]

**Framework-level QA display.**
QA messages of the same color are now sorted by their underlying score, so
the lowest (most concerning) score in each color band is easy to spot in the
weblog accordion instead of being interleaved arbitrarily; this shipped as
part of the broader SD QA-aggregation project below and currently applies to
SD-only stages ([PIPE-2988](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2988)).

### ALMA SD (`hsd_calimage` order)

**Cross-stage QA-message aggregation and formatting.** The single largest
QA/weblog effort this cycle: a common aggregator/formatter was rolled out,
stage by stage, so that QA messages sharing the same underlying metric and
score are combined into one aggregated message (with a complete
`TargetDataSelection`) instead of being listed once per MS/field/spw, making
the weblog accordion and AQUA report far less repetitive for large,
multi-source, multi-EB datasets. It landed in
{func}`hsd_baseline <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_baseline>`
([PIPE-3054](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3054)),
{func}`hsd_applycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_applycal>`
([PIPE-3055](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3055)),
{func}`hsd_imaging <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_imaging>`
([PIPE-3104](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3104)),
{func}`hsd_k2jycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_k2jycal>`,
{func}`hsd_atmcor <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_atmcor>`, and `hsd_blflag` together
([PIPE-3143](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3143)), and finally
{func}`hsd_skycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_skycal>`, which needed its own
ticket because its nested-aggregation QA structure didn't fit the common
scheme directly ([PIPE-3152](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3152)).

![Aggregated QA-message accordion for hsd_imaging, combining per-field/spw messages sharing the same metric and score][pipe3104_qaaccordion]

**{func}`hsd_skycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_skycal>` QA and weblog.** Beyond
the common-formatter rollout above, the Elevation Difference vs. Time plot
was showing flagged OFF_SOURCE data (a side effect of CAS-14752 adding fully
flagged solutions to the sky caltable so `applycal` could flag corresponding
ON_SOURCE data) — flagged solutions are now excluded from the plot
([PIPE-3198](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3198)), and a QA-score
crash (`zero-size array to reduction operation maximum`) that occurred when
an elevation-difference array ended up empty — e.g. all PM01 ON_SOURCE data
flagged for a field while OFF_SOURCE stayed valid — is now handled by
skipping the score instead of crashing
([PIPE-3199](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3199)).

![Elevation Difference vs. Time plot fix: flagged OFF_SOURCE points no longer shown][pipe3198_elevfix]

**{func}`hsd_k2jycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_k2jycal>` weblog.** A message
claiming the Jy/K database had been successfully queried was appearing even
when `dbservice=False` and no query had actually been made; the caltable
status is now correctly reported as unset in that case
([PIPE-3146](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3146)).

**{func}`hsd_applycal <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_applycal>` weblog.** The
amplitude-difference (XX−YY) vs. frequency plot filter — which hides panels
with no valid data, based on matching plot attributes against QA messages
that report "fully flagged" — had to be re-synced after the PIPE-3055
QA-message rewording, since the filter was comparing against the old message
text and some panels were coming up empty again
([PIPE-3194](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3194)).

**{func}`hsd_baseline <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_baseline>` QA.** Beyond
aggregation, two QA-detection bugs were fixed: neither the "wide line" nor
"edge line" QA warning was firing in cases where the baseline plots clearly
showed such lines — the representative line width now uses the 75th
percentile of the detected cluster (rather than a value more easily skewed
narrow) and properly accounts for flagged edge channels
([PIPE-2959](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2959)); and several QA
messages were showing real (per-MS) spw ids and MS names where virtual spw
ids would be more meaningful for multi-EB datasets with varying real-spw
assignments, or vice versa — messages were reconciled to consistently prefer
virtual spws where appropriate
([PIPE-3161](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3161)).

**{func}`hsd_imaging <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_imaging>` QA and weblog.** Edge
channels and ATM-line-overlapping channels were producing false-positive QA
warnings in both the contamination-plot QA
([PIPE-2946](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2946)) and the
missed-line-channel diagnostic QA
([PIPE-3092](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3092)); both now exclude
those channel ranges from consideration, reusing the same masked-pixel and
ATM-line-deviation-mask logic already used elsewhere. A new QA score
compares observed to theoretical image RMS (yellow outside a configurable
`x1`–`x2` ratio window, tentatively 0.9–1.6)
([PIPE-2958](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2958)). The
"possible missed line channels" diagnostic-plot section now explains its
"single peak" vs. "extended" detection thresholds and legend colors directly
in the weblog text, and shows an explicit "no significant missed line
detected" message instead of an empty section when nothing is found
([PIPE-3047](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3047)); a related
`IndexError` when the detected "representative" line range extended beyond
valid channel bounds is now clamped rather than crashing plot generation
([PIPE-3109](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3109)), and a second,
similar `IndexError` during channel-map-plot generation was fixed the same
way ([PIPE-3160](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3160)). Finally, the
AQUA report could list two targets as `IsRepresentative = True` for SD data;
the representative source is now taken strictly from the SchedBlock summary
table instead of falling back to "first science target" when the EB didn't
observe it ([PIPE-3138](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3138)).

![hsd_imaging missed-line-channel diagnostic plot, now with an explanatory legend][pipe3047_missedline]

**{func}`hsd_exportdata <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_exportdata>` weblog.** A
renderer wiring bug (the module was pointing at the generic super-renderer
instead of its own custom renderer) meant the `hsd_exportdata` weblog page
wasn't being generated properly; fixed by pointing at the correct renderer
([PIPE-3192](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-3192)).

**{func}`hsd_flagdata <pipeline.hsd.cli.hsd_flagdata>` message consistency.**
A pointing-outlier log message reported its separation in "arcsec" while the
matching QA-score message (correctly) used "deg" for the same number —
the log message unit label is now fixed to match
([PIPE-2920](https://open-jira.nrao.edu/browse/PIPE-2920)).
